title: The Full Chart of فِعْل الْأَمْر and النَّهْي — One Qur'ānic Command for Every Form
summary: Realising the lesson had quietly introduced the rest of the paradigm, the teacher puts up the complete chart for فِعْل الْأَمْر. Unlike the other verbs it has only six cells, all second person: اِذْهَبْ، اِذْهَبَا، اِذْهَبُوا، اِذْهَبِي، اِذْهَبْنَ. Each form is then matched to a command in the Qur'ān — the dual to Mūsā and Hārūn, the feminine singular to the soul in Sūrat al-Fajr, the feminine plural to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ — and النَّهْي is shown to follow the identical chart with لَا in front.
key_points: The فِعْل الْأَمْر chart is the simplest of the verb charts: only six forms, and all of them second person, since a command is by nature addressed to someone.
The forms for ذَهَبَ: اِذْهَبْ (one male), اِذْهَبَا (two, of either gender), اِذْهَبُوا (group of males), اِذْهَبِي (one female), اِذْهَبْنَ (group of females).
The dual اِذْهَبَا serves both genders, so there is nothing extra to memorise there.
The feminine singular is formed by adding a yāʾ — اِذْهَبِي، اُدْخُلِي، اِرْجِعِي — and the feminine plural by adding a nūn — اِذْهَبْنَ، اُذْكُرْنَ، أَقِمْنَ.
النَّهْي follows exactly the same chart with لَا placed in front: لَا تَذْهَبْ، لَا تَذْهَبَا، لَا تَذْهَبُوا، لَا تَذْهَبِي، لَا تَذْهَبْنَ.
نَفْس is feminine although it carries no feminine marker, which is why Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ addresses the soul with the feminine اِرْجِعِي and فَادْخُلِي in Sūrat al-Fajr.
تَعَالَ (come) belongs to a different verb pattern but takes the same endings: تَعَالَ، تَعَالِي، تَعَالَوْا، تَعَالَيْنَ. It is heard constantly in the Ḥaram — تَعَالَ، تَعَالَ.
In the Qur'ān the masculine plural form of address generally includes women as well, as in يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ.
يَد is usually translated as hand, but arm is often the better rendering, as in the wuḍū' āyah where the washing reaches the elbows.
جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم keeps taking a kasra in place of the accusative fatḥa: اِقْرَأِ الْمَجَلَّاتِ.
خُبْز is the bread itself, while the مَصْدَر خَبْز is the act of making it.

Vocabulary: مُوسَى (razor), سِكِّين (knife) with حَادّ (sharp), لَحْم (meat), طَرِيق (a road or passageway — in Saudi one hears الطَّرِيق shouted to mean clear the way), لَا أَدْرِي (I don't know), and تَبَرُّج (going out displaying one's beauty).
The نَهْي keeps the jazm at the end — لَا تَدْخُلْ، لَا تَسْمَعْ — which is what separates a prohibition from a statement.
questions: [00:09:00] Q: Are there other examples of the command addressed to a female in the Qur'ān? — A: Several, including اِرْجِعِي and فَادْخُلِي in Sūrat al-Fajr addressed to the soul, and وَاسْتَغْفِرِي in the story of Yūsuf عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام.
[00:10:00] Q: Is the last āyah of that sūrah one of these forms? — A: That one is a different form of command; the plural feminine examples are in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, as with فَتَعَالَيْنَ and أَقِمْنَ.
[00:15:00] Q: Isn't the fatḥa on تَعَالِي a mistake? — A: Yes. تَعَالِي is the feminine; تَعَالَ is for a single male. The verb has a different pattern but the same idea applies.
[00:19:00] Q: Who is being addressed here, males or females? — A: Females — hence اذْهَبْنَ، وَاعْبُدْنَ، وَاسْجُدْنَ with the nūn.
[00:21:00] Q: Does the masculine plural in the Qur'ān exclude women? — A: No. Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ generally addresses the masculine plural, and it includes women automatically.
[00:24:00] Q: Why not use the form meaning I am eating? — A: Because you are telling them to eat, so the command form is needed.
[00:24:00] Q: Is خُبْز the act of making bread? — A: The مَصْدَر خَبْز is the act; خُبْز is the bread itself.
[00:29:14] Q: Why is it الْمَجَلَّاتِ with a kasra? — A: The same rule as before: جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم takes a kasra where a fatḥa would be due.
[00:34:05] Q: Does طَرِيقَة mean the way, as in a method? — A: It can, but its basic sense is a road or passageway.

quiz.q: How many forms does the فِعْل الْأَمْر chart contain, and in which person?
options: Six, all in the second person
Nine, in the second and third persons
Three, in the second person only
quiz.a: The teacher compared it to a tic-tac-toe board: six cells, all second person, since a command is addressed to someone.
اِذْهَبَا is the dual, and it serves both genders — as in اذْهَبَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ to Mūsā and Hārūn عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام.

quiz.q: How is the command addressed to a single female formed?
quiz.a: اِذْهَبِي، اُدْخُلِي، اِرْجِعِي — the yāʾ marks the feminine singular.

quiz.q: And to a group of females?
quiz.a: اِذْهَبْنَ، اُذْكُرْنَ، أَقِمْنَ — the nūn, as throughout the passage addressing the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

quiz.q: Why does Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ address the soul with the feminine اِرْجِعِي?
options: Because it is addressing women specifically
Because نَفْس is feminine even without a feminine marker
Because it is in the dual
quiz.a: نَفْس belongs to the set of words that are feminine with no tāʾ marbūṭah, like شَمْس and نَار.

quiz.q: How is النَّهْي chart related to the الْأَمْر chart?
options: It is the same set of forms with لَا in front and the مُضَارِع kept jazm
quiz.a: لَا تَذْهَبْ، لَا تَذْهَبَا، لَا تَذْهَبُوا، لَا تَذْهَبِي، لَا تَذْهَبْنَ — the same paradigm negated.

quiz.q: What is the feminine singular of تَعَالَ?
quiz.a: تَعَالَ for one male, تَعَالِي for one female, تَعَالَوْا for a group of males, تَعَالَيْنَ for a group of females.

quiz.q: In the wuḍū' āyah, what is the better translation of أَيْدِي?
quiz.a: The teacher noted that arm is often the better rendering of يَد, and the āyah specifies up to the elbows.

quiz.q: What is the difference between خُبْز and خَبْز?
options: خُبْز is the bread; خَبْز is the مَصْدَر, the act of making it
خُبْز is the act; خَبْز is the bread
quiz.a: A مَصْدَر names the act, so خَبْز is the baking while خُبْز is the loaf.

quiz.q: What does طَرِيق mean, as heard shouted in Saudi traffic?
options: A road or way — in effect, clear the road
quiz.a: Its basic sense is a road or passageway, used that way to ask someone to move aside.

quran_examples.translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
quran_examples.note: The dual form اِذْهَبَا, addressed to Mūsā and Hārūn عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَام — the same āyah met earlier in the singular, now in the dual.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ اهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww
quran_examples.translation: He said: Descend from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others.
quran_examples.note: A second dual command, addressed to Ādam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام and his wife; هَبَطَ means to descend.

quran_examples.arabic: اذْهَبُوا بِقَمِيصِي هَٰذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِ أَبِي يَأْتِ بَصِيرًا
quran_examples.transliteration: idhhabū bi-qamīṣī hādhā fa-alqūhu ʿalā wajhi abī yaʾti baṣīrā
quran_examples.translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing.
quran_examples.note: The masculine plural اِذْهَبُوا, spoken by Yūsuf عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام to his brothers.

quran_examples.arabic: ارْجِعُوا إِلَىٰ أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا يَا أَبَانَا إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ
quran_examples.transliteration: irjiʿū ilā abīkum fa-qūlū yā abānā inna bnaka saraq
quran_examples.translation: Return to your father and say: O our father, indeed your son has stolen.
quran_examples.note: Another masculine plural from the same story, which the teacher placed beside اُقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ and اطْرَحُوهُ to show the wāw of the plural.

quran_examples.arabic: ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً ۝ فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي ۝ وَادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي
quran_examples.transliteration: irjiʿī ilā rabbiki rāḍiyatan marḍiyyah, fa-dkhulī fī ʿibādī, wa-dkhulī jannatī
quran_examples.translation: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. And enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise.
quran_examples.note: Three feminine singular commands in a row, addressed to the نَفْس — the teacher's proof that نَفْس is treated as feminine.

quran_examples.arabic: يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا ۚ وَاسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنبِكِ
quran_examples.transliteration: yūsufu aʿriḍ ʿan hādhā, wa-staghfirī li-dhanbik
quran_examples.translation: Yūsuf, turn away from this; and you, ask forgiveness for your sin.
quran_examples.note: One āyah carrying both forms at once: أَعْرِضْ to a single male and وَاسْتَغْفِرِي to a single female.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزْوَاجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ
quran_examples.transliteration: yā ayyuhā al-nabiyyu qul li-azwājika in kuntunna turidna al-ḥayāta al-dunyā wa-zīnatahā fa-taʿālayna umattiʿkunna
quran_examples.translation: O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will give you a provision.
quran_examples.note: The feminine plural تَعَالَيْنَ, with its nūn — and تُرِدْنَ beside it showing the same ending on the مُضَارِع.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَىٰ وَأَقِمْنَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتِينَ الزَّكَاةَ وَأَطِعْنَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-qarna fī buyūtikunna wa-lā tabarrajna tabarruja al-jāhiliyyati al-ūlā wa-aqimna al-ṣalāta wa-ātīna al-zakāta wa-aṭiʿna llāha wa-rasūlah
quran_examples.translation: And remain in your houses, and do not display yourselves as in the former times of ignorance, and establish prayer, and give zakāh, and obey Allah and His Messenger.
quran_examples.note: A run of feminine plural commands and one feminine plural نَهْي — لَا تَبَرَّجْنَ — which the teacher used to show that the chart's nūn runs through both الْأَمْر and النَّهْي.

quran_examples.arabic: قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ
quran_examples.transliteration: qul yā ahla al-kitābi taʿālaw ilā kalimatin sawāʾin baynanā wa-baynakum
quran_examples.translation: Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you.
quran_examples.note: The masculine plural تَعَالَوْا. The teacher cautioned against reading this as interfaith equivalence: it invites the People of the Book to weigh their shared claim to tawḥīd and so to consider Islam.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-qāla alladhīna kafarū lā tasmaʿū li-hādhā al-qurʾāni wa-lghaw fīh
quran_examples.translation: And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'ān, and speak noisily during it.
quran_examples.note: A masculine plural نَهْي matching the exercise's لَا تَسْمَعْ; لَغَا، يَلْغُو is to speak without benefit.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ يَا ابْنَ أُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأْسِي
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla ya-bna umma lā taʾkhudh bi-liḥyatī wa-lā bi-raʾsī
quran_examples.translation: He said: O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head.
quran_examples.note: The exact phrase from the exercise, spoken by Hārūn عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام to Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام on his return from the mountain — a singular نَهْي with the jazm.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطَانَ ۖ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّا
quran_examples.transliteration: yā abati lā taʿbudi al-shayṭān, inna al-shayṭāna kāna li-l-raḥmāni ʿaṣiyyā
quran_examples.translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful.
quran_examples.note: Ibrāhīm عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام to his father, the sentence the class read in the exercise; the jazm of لَا تَعْبُدْ shows as a kasra before the following alif.
